title: Agentic Coding
description: How to build LLM agents: from a single model call to multi-agent systems that review their own work.

lessons.title: LLM Basics
lessons.summary: Tokens, next-token prediction, chat messages, context windows and why the API is stateless.

lessons.title: The Agent Loop
lessons.summary: An agent is a model in a loop: decide, act, observe the result, repeat until done.

lessons.title: Tool Calling
lessons.summary: Describing tools with schemas, how the model requests a call, and how results flow back.

lessons.title: Structured Output
lessons.summary: Getting JSON that matches a schema, and validating it before your code trusts it.

lessons.title: Multi-Agent Orchestration
lessons.summary: Splitting work across specialised agents, routing with a supervisor, and sharing state.

lessons.title: Reflection and Self-Correction
lessons.summary: A reviewer agent checks proposals, sends them back with a critique, and the loop stays bounded.

misconceptions.belief: The model remembers earlier calls and conversations by itself.
The model looks answers up in a database or copies them from its training data.
The model can run code or carry out actions inside itself.
If the prompt or schema asks for something, the model's output is guaranteed to comply.
The model carries out the actions it chooses, so an action's result comes straight from the model.
An agent stops after one action; the action's result is the final answer.
The model always knows when it is done, so the loop needs no iteration cap.
Whichever agent requests a tool also executes it, inside the model or the supervisor.
The model learns what a tool does by reading its source code.
Free text is as reliable as structured output for passing data between programs or agents.
Models can't read or write JSON reliably at all.
In a strict schema, a field that may have no value should be optional or left out.
Invalid model output can be patched with defaults and used.
Each agent keeps its own memory that the other agents can read.
The supervisor hands work to agents at random.
Shared state can only hold a small fixed number of items.
Reflection means the same agent repeating or re-reading its answer.
Review loops need no cap because retries cost nothing.
Code checks make a reviewer model unnecessary.
